title: Consent Layer
definition: A layer that enables users to control which data is shared with which peers.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a digital lock on your data. Only people you choose can see it, and they need the right key.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A consent layer is a system that uses cryptography to enforce user-controlled data sharing policies. This includes partitioning data and limiting access to specific fields or directories.
difficulty_levels.expert: A consent layer is a critical component of a privacy-preserving peer-to-peer system. It enables users to control which data is shared with which peers, while also preserving data privacy and security. This requires developing both agent-level tools (e.g., partitioning and access control) and application-level interfaces (e.g., search and query).

extra_fields.insight: Both CADMIES and Atlas can build consent layers to address privacy concerns. This requires developing both agent-level tools and application-level interfaces.
